tour.title: Project Overview: What Is the Auki SDK?
tour.description: The README is the best starting point: it frames the five questions the SDK answers — Identity (who is this peer?), Spatial (where is it?), Temporal (when did this happen?), Networking (how do peers find each other?), and Tokenomics (how is coordination incentivized?). Reading it establishes the vocabulary for everything that follows and shows how the crate map maps to each question.

tour.title: Workspace Structure: The Cargo Workspace
tour.description: The root Cargo.toml declares the entire mono-repo: every Rust crate, Python PyO3 extension, and Swift UniFFI binding is listed here as a workspace member. Understanding which crates exist and how they are grouped gives you the scaffolding before diving into any individual crate.

tour.title: Identity Layer: Wallets and Ed25519 Key Pairs
tour.description: Every peer in the Auki network is identified by a Wallet — an Ed25519 signing key pair. The auki-identity crate provides the Wallet type, child-key derivation for creating sub-identities, and CreationCert issuance and verification so that ownership of a public key can be cryptographically proven. This is the foundational primitive that all higher layers build on.

tour.title: Content Addressing: JCS Canonicalization and XXH3 Hashing
tour.description: Before a document can be signed or hashed deterministically it must be serialized in a canonical order. auki-jcs wraps the RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme so that any serde_json::Value produces identical bytes everywhere. auki-hash then takes those bytes and produces a 32-character lowercase hex fingerprint using XXH3-128. Together these two crates underpin every content-addressed registry entry and manifest in the SDK.

tour.title: Spatial Primitives: Geometry and Coordinate Frames
tour.description: Spatial computing requires a precise treatment of coordinate systems. auki-geometry provides axis-handedness conversions, spatial-transform composition, quaternion utilities, and property-based tests. auki-layout pairs with it by providing deterministic filesystem-path helpers so that every registry entry — sensor, clock, frame, detector — lands at a predictable location on disk.

tour.title: Time Layer: Session Clock and NTP-Style Synchronization
tour.description: Distributed sensor fusion requires that all peers agree on a common clock. auki-time collects NTP round-trip samples, estimates the offset between a local monotonic clock and network-consensus UTC, and exposes a SessionClock that tags every registry entry with a content-addressed clock reference. TimeTransform records make the offset auditable and reproducible for offline analysis.

tour.title: Registries and Logs: Persistent Sensor Catalog and Append-Only Storage
tour.description: Before streaming data, a peer must declare what sensors it has. auki-registry provides typed, content-addressed registry-entry types for cameras, rangefinders, RF radios, audio, joint encoders, clocks, coordinate frames, and detectors, each serialized with JCS and stored atomically to disk. auki-logs then provides the append-only time-segmented binary log engine that stores the actual sensor payloads, and auki-manifests describes each log's schema so consumers can parse it without out-of-band documentation.

tour.title: Wire Protocol: Protobuf Sensor Data Types
tour.description: All sensor data that crosses the network is encoded as Protobuf. The stream.proto file defines the /auki/stream/0.2.0 substream protocol — StreamRequest, StreamManifest, StreamEntry, and the top-level StreamMessage discriminator — making it the single source of truth for the cross-language wire format. auki-datatypes wraps the prost-generated Rust types and adds LogPayload trait implementations and round-trip tests.

tour.title: Session Layer: Peer Identity and Data Collection Sessions
tour.description: The auki-session crate assembles the primitives into the local peer lifecycle. A Peer registers its coordinate frames, sensors, and detectors to the registry. A Session then creates the time-segmented log files for each registered resource and provides methods to append sensor, pose, time-transform, and detection payloads while writing manifests to disk. This is the layer that turns a raw hardware setup into a named, addressable, and archivable data source.

tour.title: Network Layer: libp2p Swarm and Peer-to-Peer Protocols
tour.description: auki-network drives the libp2p swarm that connects peers over TCP and QUIC with Noise encryption and Yamux multiplexing. Its network_runtime.rs implements all custom substream protocols: join, heartbeat, info, resources catalog, registry lookup, stream subscription, and browser-session bridging. The crate also defines PeerIdentity, SessionHandle, and Capability — the types that name each peer and describe what it can do.

tour.title: Domain Layer: Cluster Management and the App-Facing API
tour.description: auki-domain is the top-level entry point for application code. ClusterManager composes the session and network layers into a single object that creates or joins p2p clusters, runs discovery and relay-based NAT traversal, arbitrates manager election via a tiebreaker protocol, and exposes the Peer/Session/Domain abstraction to callers. The auki-domain-relay crate pairs with it by providing a Circuit Relay v2 server so browser peers behind NAT can connect.

tour.title: Diagnostic App: A Reference Native Peer Implementation
tour.description: The diagnostic-app is the reference implementation that shows how to wire all the layers together for a real running peer. Its sdk_runtime.rs builds an SdkRuntime facade that manages identity, the libp2p swarm, and the domain join/leave lifecycle on a dedicated Tokio thread, then broadcasts tick reports to an egui front-end. Reading it alongside the auki-sdk-app-builder skill gives a concrete mental model for building your own native application.

tour.title: Browser SDK: WASM and TypeScript Peer
tour.description: Browser peers participate in the same libp2p network via WebRTC and WebSocket transports. The auki-network-browser-wasm crate exposes a BrowserDomainSession wasm-bindgen class that handles discovery, relay-based join, and sensor subscription entirely from a browser tab. The auki-domain-browser TypeScript library wraps it with the same Peer/Session/Domain contract and provides the createBrowserDomainPeer factory as the single entry point for web applications.

tour.title: Python Bindings: PyO3 Robot Producers
tour.description: Python robot producers (e.g. ROS nodes) use the SDK through a set of PyO3/maturin extension modules. The auki_domain Python module is the primary entry point — it re-exports ClusterManager and related types through a Tokio async runtime bridge. Additional modules cover datatypes, geometry, identity, layout, logs, manifests, registry, and session, each generated from the corresponding Rust crate with maturin.

tour.title: Swift Bindings and CI: iOS Consumers and Automation
tour.description: iOS and macOS consumers use the SDK through UniFFI Swift bindings. auki-identity-swift and auki-network-swift expose Wallet identity and the full network peer lifecycle — liveness events, heartbeat timestamps, and all five sensor stream types — as idiomatic Swift APIs. The wiki-mirror CI workflow rounds out the picture by automatically publishing the docs/wiki directory to GitHub Wiki on every merge to develop, keeping documentation in sync with the code.
